en: A single fixed pulley on a flagpole only changes the direction of your pull and does not reduce the force needed to lift the flag.
Static friction is the force that keeps a heavy wooden box from sliding down a slightly tilted ramp before it actually starts moving.
In a vacuum with no air resistance, a heavy bowling ball and a light feather will hit the ground at the exact same time when dropped.
A standard bar magnet will strongly attract a piece of pure nickel and a piece of cobalt, not just objects made of iron.
When a flashlight is turned on, electric charges flow in a complete loop and are not consumed or used up by the lightbulb.
Sunlight reaches Earth by traveling as an electromagnetic wave through the empty vacuum of space, meaning light does not need air to move.
Sound waves travel much faster through a solid steel railway track than through surrounding air because the steel particles are packed tightly together.
When you hold a cold ice cube, thermal energy actually flows from your warmer hand into the ice, rather than coldness flowing into your hand.
A rolling skateboard eventually stops because friction converts its kinetic energy into thermal energy, meaning the energy is transformed rather than destroyed.
Using a long metal crowbar to lift a rock decreases the required input force by making you push over a longer distance, keeping total work constant.
The north-seeking pole of a compass needle points toward Earth's geographic North Pole because that geographic location is actually a magnetic south pole.
A red apple does not produce red light, but instead reflects red wavelengths from the sun while absorbing all other visible light colors.
